body:
Fix the escalation scan's blind spot for credentials proposals whose proposing verb sits inside the matched phrase.

What it is:
- Add a credentials entry to _PLAN_DIRECT_ACTIONS mirroring the existing data-migration and authorisation direct-action entries, spelling every verb inflection literally per the #1681/#1722 convention.
- Acceptance pair for funnel.plan_escalation_matches: `Rotate the deploy credentials during cutover.` returns a credentials hit, and `We will rotate the API key before the deploy.` keeps returning a credentials hit.
- Add a true-proposal regression fixture for the verb-inside-phrase shape and a guard test asserting every category that can carry its own verb has a direct-action table entry.
- Verify with `python3 -m pytest`.

Rejected:
- Broadening generic verb-proximity matching instead of a category-specific direct table, because it would re-admit non-proposals that #1643 named non-proposals and that still over-escalate per #1679.
- Stemming or lemmatizing verbs instead of spelling every inflection, because it breaks the explicit-inflection convention from #1681 and #1722 and risks matching unreviewed forms.
- Leaving the miss because #1721 softened a scan-only hit to a tier raise, because the miss still routes a real credentials change to standard-tier review.
- Folding this into #1722, because #1722 is scoped to credentials and data-migration verb inflections while this adds a missing credentials direct table.

body:
One TickTick Open API transport for operational alerts, shared by command-center and member repos

What it is:
One shared sender for operational failure alerts through the TickTick Open API, called by command-center and member repos through thin adapters, running in both Mac local runs with Keychain-held credentials and GitHub Actions runs with the existing authorized secret. It covers verified refresh-token rotation continuity in both runtimes including durable usability of any rotated refresh token in later Actions runs, a concurrency-safe uncertain-send path leaving exactly one TickTick task under timeout retries, overlapping retries, unknown outcomes, simultaneous Mac and Actions sends, lease expiry, and delayed TickTick visibility beyond the bounded reconcile window, with live tests against real TickTick behavior proving the single-task outcome. Scope stays operational alerts only, and the work changes no credentials, settings, integrations, permissions, or spending; where present access cannot durably persist a rotated token, the transport fails safely.

Ticket-sized work:
1. Define the shared send interface, caller adapter shape, operational-alert-only guardrails, rollout assumptions, and rollback behavior.
2. Specify and verify the dual-runtime auth and refresh path, including how a rotated refresh token stays durable and usable for later runs in each runtime.
3. Establish with present-access evidence whether the existing authorized Actions credential and permission can persist the rotated token for later runs, and specify the safe-failure behavior when that access is absent.
4. Specify the shared cross-runtime coordination contract for sends, covering acquisition, lease expiry, retries after unknown outcomes, and handling of delayed visibility beyond the bounded reconcile window.
5. Specify transient-state rules for any local retry spool or omit the spool, covering ownership, retention, cleanup, crash recovery, and unknown-outcome handling consistent with GitHub as state of record.
6. Specify and run live tests against real TickTick behavior proving one task remains under overlapping and delayed retries, simultaneous Mac and Actions sends, unknown outcomes, and lease expiry with retries.

Rejected:
- Pre-create title lookup alone as deduplication, because send-back reasoning falsified it: overlapping timeout retries and late-visible prior creates can still leave duplicates.
- Treating a proposed future live test as evidence of present Actions secret-write access, because send-back reasoning states it is not evidence of present access.
- Adding a new credential, expanded permission, new integration, or spending change for rotation write-back, because the send-backs authorize none.
- Verifying rotation in only one runtime, because the send-backs require verified continuity in both local Keychain runs and Actions runs.
- Keeping a local retry spool as state of record or without ownership, retention, cleanup, crash recovery, and unknown-outcome rules reconciled with GitHub as state, because it conflicts with the GitHub-is-state rule.
- Relying on a bounded reconcile window alone while leaving delayed visibility beyond the bound unhandled, because the send-backs require no duplicate remains in that case.
- Broadening the sender beyond operational alerts, because the scope is fixed to operational alerts only.
- Per-repo duplicate senders instead of one shared transport with thin adapters, because it duplicates auth, rotation, and deduplication behavior across callers.

## Premises

- TickTick Open API can create operational-alert tasks from Mac local runs and GitHub Actions runs. (label: inferred; evidence: nateprich-projects/command-center#2029 thread 2026-10-01T16:29:31Z cites TickTick task creation and tests against real TickTick behavior.)
- Mac local runs hold TickTick credentials in Keychain and Actions runs use an existing authorized secret. (label: inferred; evidence: nateprich-projects/command-center#2029 thread 2026-09-30T23:02:02Z and 2026-10-01T18:43:14Z assert local Keychain runs and existing authorized Actions secret.)
- TickTick refresh tokens can rotate and any rotated token must remain durable and usable for later runs in each runtime. (label: inferred; evidence: nateprich-projects/command-center#2029 thread 2026-10-01T16:29:31Z requires verified rotation continuity and durable rotated-token storage in both runtimes.)
- Timeout retries, overlapping retries, unknown outcomes, simultaneous Mac and Actions sends, lease expiry, and delayed TickTick visibility beyond the bounded reconcile window can otherwise leave duplicate tasks. (label: inferred; evidence: nateprich-projects/command-center#2029 thread 2026-10-01T21:03:16Z lists those cases including delayed visibility beyond the 10-minute bound.)
- GitHub is the state of record for shared send coordination and any transient retry state. (label: inferred; evidence: nateprich-projects/command-center#2029 thread 2026-10-01T18:43:14Z cites the GitHub-is-state rule for spool reconciliation.)

Proposed class: Improve

## Risk rationale

- credentials: Plan handles TickTick refresh tokens and durable write-back of rotated tokens to the Actions secret.
- authorisation: Plan depends on whether the existing Actions credential and permission can update the secret.
- concurrency: Plan must leave one task under simultaneous Mac and Actions sends, overlapping retries, unknown outcomes, and lease expiry.

## Decided from precedent

- TickTick receives exactly operational failure alerts as genuine tasks, never ideas or backlog items. (source: plan.md Surfaces: TickTick receives exactly one thing: operational failure alerts, which are genuine tasks.)

## Decided by the agent

- The Actions run overwrites the existing authorized Actions secret in place with the rotated refresh token using only its existing identity, so later runs read the new value. (rejected: Persist the rotated token to a new secret, repo file, or local artifact, or mint a new credential to perform the write.; One in-place secret keeps GitHub as the state of record with no second source and stays within the no-new-credential and never-commit-secrets bounds.)
- Evidence is a recorded run where the existing Actions identity updates the existing secret and a later run reads it back with values redacted, and without it the sender retains the prior token and raises a non-secret failure without write-back. (rejected: Treat planned future tests or vendor docs as present-access proof, and on missing access retry the write or cache the token outside the secret.; Only an observed write-then-read proves present permission can persist rotation, and retaining the old token with a visible failure avoids silent loss or insecure fallback.)
- Run a live rotation drill in each runtime that forces a refresh, persists via that runtime path, then proves a following run authenticates with the rotated token. (rejected: Verify rotation in one runtime only, or from documentation and mocks without a live refresh and follow-on auth in each runtime.; Separate live drills catch Keychain versus secret persistence gaps, and the follow-on auth proves the rotated token remains usable for later runs.)
- Use one GitHub-stored alert claim per alert with atomic first-writer acquisition and TTL lease expiry plus reconcile-before-takeover. (rejected: Allow independent Mac and Actions sends reconciled later by TickTick title lookup.; GitHub is the only shared state both runtimes already write, and send-backs falsified title-lookup-alone because overlapping and late-visible creates still duplicate.)
- Retries must re-acquire the same GitHub claim lease and reconcile TickTick state before any re-create, holding the lease through confirmation. (rejected: Retry by immediately re-creating the TickTick task on timeout or unknown response.; An unknown outcome may hide a succeeded create, so only lease-gated reconcile-before-create prevents a second task under overlapping retries.)
- The lease holder renews the GitHub claim past the bounded window until TickTick confirms exactly one task, deleting any duplicate before release. (rejected: Release the claim at the bounded reconcile deadline and leave late-appearing duplicates in place.; Send-backs require no duplicate remains beyond the bound and falsified bounded-reconcile-alone, so release must wait on single-task confirmation.)
- Set the bounded reconcile window to 10 minutes for duplicate detection and delayed-visibility handling. (rejected: Use an unbounded window or an unspecified length with no testable bound.; A fixed 10-minute bound preserves the value already named in the thread while keeping reconcile bounded and live-testable.)
- Omit any transient local retry spool so all send retry and unknown-outcome state lives only in the shared GitHub coordination record. (rejected: Keep a Mac-local transient spool with defined ownership retention cleanup crash recovery and unknown-outcome rules.; Only GitHub state is visible to both Mac and Actions so a local spool cannot prevent cross-runtime duplicates and adds crash and retention failure modes.)
- Require five live tests against real TickTick each proving exactly one task remains under overlapping retries delayed visibility simultaneous Mac-and-Actions sends unknown outcomes and lease-expiry retries. (rejected: Accept mocked TickTick tests or a single happy-path live create without overlap delay cross-runtime unknown-outcome and lease cases.; Only live concurrent cross-runtime delayed and lease-expiry cases can falsify duplicate creation under real TickTick visibility and timing behavior.)
- House the transport once in command-center as canonical source with thin caller adapters in member repos invoking the shared send interface. (rejected: Copy the full sender into each member repo with independent auth and retry logic.; One canonical source prevents drift in rotation and deduplication while thin adapters preserve caller independence.)
- Record no credential, permission, integration, or spending changes with rollback to prior per-caller sends if verification fails. (rejected: Assume new access can be provisioned during rollout with forward-only fixes and no rollback.; Send-backs forbid new access and scope change, so rollout must be reversible without widening authority.)
